source.title: Gmail Trigger's error handling keeps the new poll back-off from ever engaging (polls every minute through 401/429)

labels.name: team:nodes
labels.description: Issue is with the Nodes team

labels.name: status:in-linear

source.body:
### Bug Description

With `N8N_SCHEDULER_POLL_TRIGGERS_ENABLED=true` and `N8N_POLLER_DURABLE_CURSORS_ENABLED=true`, a failing poll trigger backs off (`poll-backoff.service.js`, which already maps 429 + Retry-After and 401/403). The Gmail Trigger never reaches it, because it catches its own API errors and returns "no new mail":

```ts
// packages/nodes-base/nodes/Google/Gmail/GmailTrigger.node.ts (same on master today)
if (this.getMode() !== 'manual') {
    nodeStaticData.lastTimeChecked ??= +now;          // set before the try, on every scheduled poll
}
...
} catch (error) {
    if (this.getMode() === 'manual' || !nodeStaticData.lastTimeChecked) {
        throw error;                                   // so this only fires for manual runs
    }
    this.logger.error(`There was a problem in '${node.name}' node in workflow '${workflow.id}': '${error.description}'`, ...);
}
...
if (!allFetchedMessages.length) {
    return null;
}
```

Because `lastTimeChecked` is set before the `try`, the rethrow only fires in manual mode, so every scheduled poll's errors are hidden. `PollTriggerTaskHandler` sees a successful empty poll and calls `recordSuccess`, never `recordFailure`. There's no back-off, no failed execution and no error workflow; the only trace is one log line per poll.

I understand the swallow-and-log was probably deliberate under the old in-memory poller, so one Gmail hiccup wouldn't stop a workflow (#5397 was closed on similar grounds). Now that the scheduler handles failures properly (back-off, cursor left in place, workflow stays active), the swallow defeats the protection the back-off was built for.

Why it matters to us: a Gmail Trigger hit `429 User-rate limit exceeded` and kept polling every minute. Each refused call pushed Gmail's Retry-After further out, and the mailbox stayed blocked for about 13 hours.

### To Reproduce

1. Enable the two settings above (`N8N_SCHEDULER_ENABLED` and `N8N_USE_WORKFLOW_PUBLICATION_SERVICE` at their default true).
2. Create a `gmailOAuth2` credential with a made-up client and access token, so Google answers 401.
3. Create a workflow with only a Gmail Trigger (typeVersion 1.4, poll every minute) using that credential, then activate it.

**Observed:**
- Activation succeeds, even though the credential can't work.
- For 6 minutes, every scheduled task finished `succeeded`, and `poller_state.consecutiveErrors` stayed `0` with `backoffUntil` null.
- No executions were saved.
- The log showed `There was a problem in 'Gmail test' node in workflow '<id>': 'undefined'` once a minute (`error.description` is undefined for this error, so the line doesn't even say what failed).

**Control:** an RSS Feed Read Trigger on the same instance, pointed at a server answering `429` with `Retry-After: 180`, logged `Poll failed; backing off`, `consecutiveErrors` went 1→3, and its polls dropped from every minute to every 4 minutes.

### Expected behavior

Gmail API errors on a scheduled poll should reach the poll back-off like other poll triggers: a 429 should honour Retry-After, and a 401/403 should get the long back-off. One option: rethrow when durable poll cursors are on (or always, now that the scheduler handles failures), and keep the log-and-continue path only for the legacy poller. Also, the log line should fall back to `error.message` when `error.description` is undefined.

### Debug Info

- Gmail Trigger typeVersion 1.4, poll mode "every minute"
- `N8N_SCHEDULER_POLL_TRIGGERS_ENABLED=true`, `N8N_POLLER_DURABLE_CURSORS_ENABLED=true`; `N8N_SCHEDULER_ENABLED` and `N8N_USE_WORKFLOW_PUBLICATION_SERVICE` at default (true)
- Docker image `docker.n8n.io/n8nio/n8n`, Postgres 16, single main instance

### Operating System

macOS 26 (Docker Desktop)

### n8n Version

2.45.5

### Node.js Version

26.12.1

### Database

PostgreSQL

### Execution mode

main (default)

### Hosting

self hosted

comments.author: goutham-valugula
comments.text: I checked the current `master` source. The scheduled Gmail path initializes `lastTimeChecked` before the poll’s outer `try`, then the catch rethrows only for manual mode or a missing cursor; otherwise it logs and continues ([GmailTrigger.node.ts](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/master/packages/nodes-base/nodes/Google/Gmail/GmailTrigger.node.ts#L341-L345) and [catch/empty result](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/master/packages/nodes-base/nodes/Google/Gmail/GmailTrigger.node.ts#L792-L811)). The poll task handler records failure from its exception path and success after a completed poll ([poll-trigger-task-handler.ts](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/master/packages/cli/src/scheduling/poll-trigger-node/poll-trigger-task-handler.ts#L150-L215)), so this swallowed exception can indeed bypass back-off as described. A focused regression test should cover a Gmail API error with durable cursors enabled and verify it reaches the scheduler failure path; the existing legacy behavior can remain conditional if needed.
